structured_output.hypothesis: If all domestic pigeon breeds descend from Columba livia and its geographic subspecies alone, genome-wide variation in every breed will nest within C. livia diversity, with no breed's ancestry derived from any other Columba species.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using the Cliv_2.1 reference to map reads and call genome-wide autosomal SNPs for all domestic breeds with public reads, an outgroup-rooted neighbour-joining or maximum-likelihood tree places 100% of breeds in one clade that also contains the wild or feral C. livia samples, with bootstrap support of at least 90% at that node. In addition, no ABBA-BABA D-statistic comparing a breed against C. livia and any other Columba species (for example C. rupestris or C. guinea) has |Z| > 3 after Bonferroni correction.
structured_output.fail_criterion: At least one domestic breed falls outside the C. livia clade, or sits closer to another Columba species than to any C. livia sample (bootstrap of at least 90%). Alternatively, a breed shows a significant excess of allele sharing with another Columba species (|Z| > 3 after Bonferroni correction) with a genome-wide admixture fraction above 5%. Either result refutes descent from C. livia alone.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'aboriginal wild stocks' means separate wild species, which are the other Columba lineages. 'Geographical sub-species' maps to wild and feral C. livia populations. 'Descended from' is read as monophyly of the breeds within C. livia plus the absence of detectable introgression from other species. The modern reinterpretation uses genome-wide SNP phylogenetics and D-statistics. Limits: this dataset's reference is a C. livia genome. The breed re-sequencing reads that decide the test are in the SRA runs linked from this assembly's BioProject (the Shapiro et al. 2013 data). Those reads must be obtained from the linked records. Introgression from other species cannot be excluded outright if outgroup genomes are sparse. Small amounts of ancient gene flow would not by themselves refute the claim.
